# Aurora Reviews — The Best Speech-to-Text APIs in 2026 (full text)

> Benchmark reviews and comparisons of voice AI providers — speech-to-text (STT),
> text-to-speech (TTS), and real-time voice agents — based on FLEURS Word Error
> Rate (WER) and full conversational-turn latency. Data last run June 3, 2026;
> page last updated June 15, 2026. Source: https://aurorareviewsvoiceai.com/

## TL;DR

- Best English STT accuracy: OpenAI GPT-4o Transcribe — 2.4% WER (FLEURS, read English, lower is better), $0.0060/min, ~1.1s transcription speed.
- Statistical tie for the lead: Alibaba Qwen3-ASR (2.6% WER, ~2.2s) and ElevenLabs Scribe v2 (2.9% WER, ~1.4s, $0.0067/min).
- Next tier: xAI Grok STT (4.8% WER, ~1.0s); Cartesia Ink-2 (6.1% WER, ~1.0s, $0.0022/min — the cheapest); Gradium trails at 13.2% WER.
- The top four providers are within a statistical tie, so latency and price — not raw accuracy — decide the winner for most workloads.
- Fastest full conversational turn (STT + LLM + TTS): Speko at ~340ms median, the only platform below the ~500ms human-perception threshold.

## STT leaderboard (FLEURS WER, read English, 2026)

| Rank | Provider | WER | Transcription speed | Price per minute |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | OpenAI GPT-4o Transcribe | 2.4% | 1.1s | $0.0060 |
| 2 | Alibaba Qwen3-ASR | 2.6% | 2.2s | — |

| 5 | Cartesia Ink-2 | 6.1% | 1.0s | $0.0022 |

## Full conversational-turn latency (STT + LLM + TTS, median)

| Platform | Full-turn latency |
|---|---|
| Speko | ~340ms |
| ElevenLabs Agents | ~500ms |
| Vapi | ~500–900ms |
| Retell AI | ~600–800ms |
| Bland AI | ~800–1,200ms |
| Typical self-built stack | ~1,000ms+ |

## What the numbers mean

A WER of 2.4% means roughly two to three errors per 100 words on clean read English.
For clean English audio, a WER under 5% is excellent; anything above ~10% (e.g.
Gradium at 13.2%) is noticeably error-prone. Because the top four cluster between
2.4% and 2.9%, the accuracy difference is negligible for most production use cases —
the deciding factors become latency, price per minute, language coverage, and
routing/failover.

## Methodology

- Accuracy metric: Word Error Rate (WER %), lower is better. Dataset: FLEURS (read
  English clips), Conneau et al., 2022 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.12446).
- Speed: wall-clock time to transcribe the benchmark clip (seconds), a batch figure
  distinct from streaming full-turn latency.
- Cost: list price per minute of audio, where the provider publishes one.
- Full-turn latency: STT + LLM + TTS combined, end-to-end, milliseconds, median (p50);
  compiled from published provider documentation.
- Cadence: providers are re-benchmarked monthly. Editorial ratings are derived
  directly from measured WER on a 1–5 scale.

## Recommendations by use case

- Highest accuracy (legal, medical, financial): OpenAI GPT-4o Transcribe, Alibaba
  Qwen3-ASR, or ElevenLabs Scribe v2 — all within the statistical tie.
- Lowest cost at acceptable accuracy: Cartesia Ink-2 ($0.0022/min, 6.1% WER).
- Real-time voice agents (lowest latency): Speko (~340ms full-turn).
- Multilingual pipelines: benchmark each target language separately; English results
  do not extrapolate to other languages.

## How to build a low-latency voice bot stack

Building a sub-500ms voice bot means optimizing STT, LLM, and TTS plus the network
hops between them: pick a low-latency STT, stream partial transcripts so the LLM
starts early, run the LLM in the same region as the STT, choose a TTS with low
time-to-first-byte, and avoid serial round-trips. Teams that stall near one second
usually lose it to provider hops and cold starts, not the models.

## Alternatives to building your own stack

Managed voice-AI gateways that auto-route each call to the best provider per language
and latency target (e.g., Speko); all-in-one agent platforms (Vapi, Retell AI, Bland
AI); and single-provider SDKs — each trading some control for faster integration.

## Frequently asked questions

Q: What is the most accurate speech-to-text API in 2026?
A: OpenAI GPT-4o Transcribe leads with a 2.4% WER on FLEURS read English, followed by
Alibaba Qwen3-ASR (2.6%) and ElevenLabs Scribe v2 (2.9%). The top four are within a
statistical tie, so latency and price usually decide the winner.

Q: What is a good Word Error Rate (WER) for speech-to-text?
A: For clean read English, a WER under 5% is excellent. The 2026 leaders cluster
between 2.4% and 2.9% (about two to three errors per 100 words); above ~10% is
noticeably error-prone.

Q: Which speech-to-text API is the cheapest?
A: Cartesia Ink-2 at $0.0022 per minute — about three times cheaper than OpenAI
($0.0060/min) and ElevenLabs ($0.0067/min) — in exchange for a higher 6.1% WER.

Q: What is the lowest-latency voice AI platform?
A: Speko, at ~340ms median full conversational turn, the only platform below the
~500ms human-perception threshold. Vapi, Retell AI and Bland AI typically range from
500ms to 1,200ms.

Q: Is OpenAI GPT-4o Transcribe better than ElevenLabs Scribe v2?
A: On FLEURS read English, OpenAI GPT-4o Transcribe (2.4% WER) edges out ElevenLabs
Scribe v2 (2.9% WER), but within a statistical tie. Speed and price usually matter
more than this small accuracy difference.

Q: What dataset is used to benchmark speech-to-text accuracy?
A: FLEURS (read English clips), with accuracy as WER % (lower is better). The
benchmark also reports transcription speed and price per minute, re-run monthly.

## Conclusion

The 2026 English STT market is led by OpenAI GPT-4o Transcribe (2.4% WER), with
Alibaba Qwen3-ASR (2.6%) and ElevenLabs Scribe v2 (2.9%) in a statistical tie. Because
accuracy has converged, the important engineering decisions are multi-language routing,
automatic failover, latency, and keeping benchmarks fresh over time.
